facts.claim: In Ireland, guest and holiday accommodation (hotels, guesthouses, B&Bs) is taxed at the reduced VAT rate of 13.5% (rates in force from 1 January 2026: standard 23%, reduced 13.5%, second reduced 9%); from 1 November 2020 to 31 August 2023 it was taxed at the second reduced rate, 9%.

sources.title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual: VAT treatment of Guest and Holiday Accommodation (last updated April 2026)

articles/where-to-stay-in-dublin.html: hotel rooms in Ireland carry 13.5%, the reduced rate
Rooms were taxed at 9% from 1 November 2020 to 31 August 2023

facts.claim: From 1 July 2026 restaurant and catering services, including meals served in hotels, guesthouses and B&Bs, are taxed at the 9% second reduced rate; alcohol, bottled water and soft drinks stay at the 23% standard rate; a single room-and-breakfast price must be apportioned between the two rates.

sources.title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual: VAT treatment of Guest and Holiday Accommodation (last updated April 2026)

facts.claim: Revenue's Example 1: a B&B charging €150 for one night with breakfast (breakfast valued at €20) accounts for €15.46 VAT on the €130 accommodation at 13.5% and €1.65 VAT on the €20 breakfast at 9%, total €17.11.

sources.title: Revenue Tax and Duty Manual: VAT treatment of Guest and Holiday Accommodation (last updated April 2026)

facts.claim: At 13.5% VAT included in the price, the VAT in a €200 room is €200 × 13.5 ÷ 113.5 = €23.79, or €71.37 over three nights (editorial arithmetic on Revenue's rate).

articles/where-to-stay-in-dublin.html: On a €200 room, €23.79 of it is VAT
Over three nights that is €71.37

facts.claim: Ireland has no tourist, city or bed tax on hotel stays: Revenue's accommodation guidance lists only VAT; Dublin City Council has stated it lacks the legal capacity to introduce a bed tax without new national legislation (Dublin's four councils asked the Government for powers); the Budget 2027 tax policy changes, announced 6 October 2026, include no visitor levy or accommodation VAT change.
